text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High rate of CUDA illegal memory access on serving-node-34. 12 errors/min, nodelabel=gpu-prod. Auto-restart triggered on 3 containers.
ryan_oncall: I'm on it. pulling logs now. which services are hitting this?
alice_nguyen: model-serving pods on that node: rf-infer-*, chat-api-2. Customers hitting tail latency spikes.
emily_sre: can we get the kernel oops / dmesg?
ryan_oncall: grabbing dmesg and container logs, sending snippet.
ryan_oncall: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:01:00.0: GPU panic: Xid 23: PID 41722: GPU access fault, reason 0x5
[ 12345.679002] cpu 3: Exception 14 (Page fault) at 0x7ffdeadbeef, ra 0xffffffff81234abc
[ 12345.679103] CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: misaligned device addr during pagewalk
```
ben_soder: that stack looks like kernel pagewalk failure rather than user OOM. probably a driver/kernel mismatch or pte race.
r: @ryan_oncall can you confirm node hasn't OOM'd?
ryan_oncall: top shows no system OOMs, memory pressure moderate. containers restarted due to SIGSEGV inside the runtime.
emily_sre: plan: cordon+drain node immediately to stop new placements, move traffic to standby pool, and disable autoscaler for that AZ while we triage.
alice_nguyen: customer impact: two high-traffic tenants saw 5-10% error rates for generation requests; fallback to smaller model deployed in region took some traffic but increased latency.
julia_support: I'll open a prioritized customer ticket and push a short status note: "We're mitigating a GPU kernel-level issue; engineering investigating. Some requests may error or be slower."
ryan_oncall: draining now: `kubectl cordon serving-node-34 && kubectl drain serving-node-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started evacuation of pods from serving-node-34 at 2026-03-17T12:08:20Z.
ben_soder: while draining, let's disable KV cache promotion on the affected model group to reduce stress (temporary config flip).
emily_sre: agreed. @alice_nguyen do that with a quick rollback in config-service.
alice_nguyen: flipped cache_promotion=false for rf-models-prod. pushing now.
ryan_oncall: extracting core from restarted container for repro. attaching gdb backtrace: `runtime: GPU::kernel.cc +0x1f2` repeated.
ben_soder: can we repro on a staging node with same kernel/driver combo? if it's a kernel pagewalk race it's sensitive to memory layout.
emily_sre: yes, set up a repro job but don't run on prod hardware. use test-pool-gpu-2 with same driver version.
ryan_oncall: repro job started, injecting synthetic traffic with long sequences.
ops-bot: incident-tracker: Incident I-2026-042 created (sev2) — kernel pagewalk illegal address on GPU nodes.
julia_support: sent customer update v1. Keeping language high-level, offering postmortem and timeline once root cause is known.
ben_soder: short-term remediation options: 1) rollback recent kernel/driver update to known-good image on that AZ, 2) set node-level GPU reset policy to soft-fallback (containers restarted) 3) patch runtime to avoid known access pattern.
emily_sre: do we have recent driver/kernel changes in the rollout?
alice_nguyen: yes, a minor NVIDIA driver push rolled out to that AZ ~3 hours before incident. rollout was ~10% of nodes in AZ.nyan_oncall: it's likely correlated. I'll rollback driver on serving-node-34 to previous package and validate.
ryan_oncall: running ansible playbook: `ansible -i hosts serving-node-34 -m shell -a "apt-get install nvidia-driver=525.89-previous"`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Driver rollback started on serving-node-34.
ben_soder: while rollback runs, enable model-level fallback route to cpu-infer pool for critical customers to avoid errors. add rate limit to reduce cost.
alice_nguyen: done — routed 40% of traffic for tenant:search-inc to cpu-infer-fallback. latency up ~2x but errors down.
julia_support: customer update v2 sent: "We've routed impacted workloads to fallback capacity and are rolling back a driver change; expect reduced errors within 30-45 minutes."
emily_sre: monitoring shows error rate dropping from 12/min to 2/min post-rollback on one node. need to watch other nodes that had the driver rollout.
ryan_oncall: scanning for other nodes with same driver version in the AZ. found 6 nodes. cordoning 2 with highest error counts, scheduling batch rollback.
ops-bot: sched-bot: Rolling batch rollback queued for nodes: serving-node-28, serving-node-34, serving-node-41. ETA 15m.
ben_soder: notify kernel/driver team with logs and repro. assign to eng-ml oncall as primary for next 4 hours.
emily_sre: assigned. adding hotpatch attempt to run a kernel config that disables aggressive pagewalk caching for GPUs as experiment on staging.
ryan_oncall: collecting incident timeline and artifacts: dmesg, container core, nvml logs, kube events. uploading to I-2026-042.
julia_support: prepping customer-impact list: affected tenants: search-inc (10k requests/min), chatty-ai (3k rps), internal-infra (low). adding mitigation note.
alice_nguyen: also filing a follow-up to consider more granular rollout gating for driver updates (canary across racks, smoke test with long-context infer).
ben_soder: if rollback stabilizes, plan for coordinated re-roll but with additional kernel debug flags enabled on a small canary.
emily_sre: OK. next steps: 1) complete rollback on affected nodes (in-progress) 2) verify telemetry for 2h 3) repro & root-cause with driver/kernel teams 4) postmortem + timeline + follow-up mitigations.
ryan_oncall: marking incident as active and oncall handoff scheduled in 2h to emily_sre. I'm moving to mitigation mode.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: serving-node-34 drain complete; pods rescheduled. node in maintenance.
julia_support: sending final short update to customers now.
emily_sre: thanks all — will lead the follow-up and postmortem once we have kernel team feedback. please attach any extra logs to the incident ticket. :shipit:"
